posts.caption: In 2021, one engineer typed one wrong command and 3.5 billion people lost the internet in a single instant. Not hacked. Not attacked. Just one wrong line of code during a routine maintenance check. Facebook's own engineers couldn't even log in to fix it, their access tools were on the same servers that just vanished. They had to physically drive to data centers and override servers by hand. One by one. 6 hours. $60 million lost every single hour. And the exact same vulnerability? Still exists right now. The internet is more fragile than you think.

2021 mein ek engineer ne ek galat command type ki aur 3.5 billion logon ka internet ek pal mein band ho gaya. Hack nahi hua. Attack nahi hua. Bas ek routine maintenance check ke dauran ek galat line of code. 6 ghante. Har ghante 60 million dollar ka nuksaan. Internet utna strong nahi jitna hum sochte hain.

There is a sound that only 2% of people can hear. Scientists have studied it for 50 years and still have no answer. It's called The Hum — and the leading theory is that it's the Earth itself vibrating at a frequency most humans aren't built to detect. A woman heard it for 11 years, moved across the country to escape it, and it followed her to the new house. Stop right now, close your eyes, and listen. What do you hear?

We call space the final frontier. But we've barely explored our own planet. Earth is stranger than anything we've found out there — and most people have no idea. From perfect solar eclipses to oceans deeper than mountains are tall, this is the planet you thought you knew.

In 1974, a man calculated the exact day he would die and spent a year preparing for it. What happened next is stranger than the prediction itself. Frank was obsessed with numerology. He told his family, quit his job, and gave away everything he owned. When the day came and went without incident, he thought he'd beaten fate. He hadn't.

Death isn't a single switch that shuts down your entire body at once. When your heart stops beating and your brain goes silent, trillions of cells inside you are still alive, desperately trying to keep themselves running. What actually happens when you die? What makes death so mysterious, and which cells are the last survivors within your body? Watch our full video to find out!

recentPosts.caption:
A beautiful tradition of respect and appreciation. ❤️ ⁠
During Bhai Tika in Nepal, women are honored by their brothers and male family members, who touch their feet and offer blessings and gifts as a gesture of love, gratitude and respect. ⁠
⁠
The ritual reflects a cultural belief in the importance of women in bringing prosperity and good fortune to the family.⁠
🎥: @sanjushreshtha

These lagoons look like they were painted onto the salt. 💛⁠
⁠
Salar de Gorbea in Chile is known for its striking yellow, green, and turquoise lagoons, set against huge stretches of white salt and reddish volcanic mountains.⁠
⁠
The colors come from the minerals, microorganisms, high salt concentrations, and volcanic activity found in this remote part of the Atacama.⁠
⁠
Getting here isn’t easy either. Salar de Gorbea sits at nearly 4,000 meters above sea level and is usually visited as part of a

In this Romanian bar, ordering a shot comes with a little extra surprise: a keg to the head! 🍻😂 ⁠
Don't worry, they provide a helmet… because apparently, that's part of the experience.⁠
🎥: @sarmiswilldoit

Le Train Bleu, @restaurantletrainbleu, inside Gare de Lyon station in Paris is a restaurant that looks more like a palace than a place to wait for your train.⁠
⁠
It was created for the 1900 World’s Fair, and its dining rooms are covered with 41 paintings, many showing the French destinations travelers could reach by train. With gold details, chandeliers and painted ceilings, it’s been a historic monument since 1972.⁠
⁠
Would you come here for lunch even if you weren’t catching a train?

In northern Mongolia, the Dukha people, also known as the Tsaatan or “Reindeer People,” have a way of life deeply connected to their reindeer and the surrounding taiga forests.⁠
For the youngest generation, learning to ride reindeer is part of growing up with their community’s traditions. ⁠
⁠
During this visit, children aged 4–8 took part in a special reindeer race, celebrating a way of life passed down through generations. A beautiful glimpse into a culture unlike any other. 🦌⁠
🎥: @yalla.sara

Photographer @dani.guindo captures the flight paths of birds across Iceland’s incredible scenery. 🐦⁠
⁠
By tracking their movements through the frame, he turns ordinary bird flights into beautiful patterns against Iceland’s dramatic natural scenery.

Some traditions are more than rituals; they're a connection to faith passed down through generations. 🙏 ⁠
⁠
At Srirangam Temple in Trichy, devotees take part in a unique practice of placing their fingers on a concrete lid and attempting to lift it, keeping a centuries-old sense of devotion and tradition alive. ⁠
🎥: @withsawaa

Some facts about the world sound completely made up, but they're actually true. 🌍⁠
⁠
How many of these did you already know? Which one surprised you the most?

At first glance, this peregrine falcon looks like he’s asking for silence. He’s in fact, taking a moment on the cliffside to clean his talons, an important part of keeping them ready for the hunt.⁠
⁠
Peregrine falcons are famous for their speed. In a hunting dive, they can reach over 200 miles per hour, which makes them widely known as the fastest animal on Earth.⁠
⁠
By: @scottsessionsphoto

Talk about travelling in style! 🌊🐌 An emperor shrimp catches a free ride on the Spanish dancer, one of the ocean’s largest sea slugs, growing up to 15 inches long. Named for its graceful, flamenco-like movements, this underwater beauty makes quite the ride for its tiny passenger. 🦐✨⁠
⁠
🎥: @scuba_moment

Tuscany looks incredible from above at sunrise. ⁠
⁠
@gabornagy_photography captured these aerial views of the Tuscan countryside in autumn, when the first light of day brings out the region’s rolling hills, winding gravel roads, and warm colors.⁠
⁠
To get these shots, he rode his road bike for 50 km along the famous Strade Bianche gravel roads in complete darkness, carrying his drone on his back to reach the perfect spots before sunrise.⁠
⁠
These photos were captured in October 2017.

A hike that feels almost unreal! ⛰️ ⁠
Harihar Fort in Maharashtra, India, sits at around 3,676 feet and is famous for its steep, narrow rock-cut steps that make the climb an unforgettable adventure. ⁠
⁠
Not for the faint-hearted, but what a view from the top! 😮⁠
🎥: @jithu_chandranc

Indris are the largest lemur species in the world, and they are known for their astonishingly loud, musical singing. Found in Madagascar, indris are among the many animals unique to the island—but their habitat is threatened. Now, to estimate the population, scientists are using a process known as passive acoustic monitoring to map the density and abundance of the endemic species.

The ketogenic diet has helped some people find relief from chronic migraines, but its restrictive nature and potential health risks make it a controversial treatment. Now, researchers are looking more closely at how rapid swings in blood sugar, which standard tests may miss, could play a role. While some patients respond better to the diet than others, experts hope their findings could lead to more personalized treatment options.
